newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close flat in shortened session.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close flat in shortened session.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended little changed on Friday as an early close for the Canadian market kept activity levels and volumes light, analysts said.

"It was an early day and everybody wanted to get out on time. That probably had a lot to do with it," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with financial analysis firm I.D.E.A. "Everybody is just waiting for the FOMC meeting on Tuesday, so I think people are pretty much square right now."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.05 to C$111.45 to yield 7.035 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 5/32 to yield 6.90 percent. The spread between the bonds was 14 basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Thursday.

The Toronto Bond Traders' Association this morning recommended an early market close ahead of the holiday weekend. Monday is Victoria Day in Canada and financial markets across the country will be closed.
The association's recommendation that the market cease trading at 1200 EDT/1600 GMT effectively meant an early close to bond trading across Canada, as most dealers are in Toronto.
Analysts said many traders had squared positions and were looking ahead to the meeting on Tuesday of the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate-setting Open Market Committee.
Opinion was divided on whether the FOMC would hike rates for a second time this year. A Fed rate hike would likely weaken the Canadian dollar and fixed-income markets.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.08 to C$103.42 to yield 6.512 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 5/32 to yield 6.69 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds narrowed to 18 basis points from 19 basis points at Thursday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 3.03 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.18 percent.
